entry.title: Beyond the Context Window: Building a Stateful 'Memory' MCP Server on Cloudflare Workers
entry.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) like Claude possess incredible reasoning capabilities, but they suffer from a critical flaw: They have no object permanence. Once you close a chat session, the "mind" is wiped. While features like "Projects" or huge context windows (200k+ tokens) help, they are temporary buffers, not true memory. They are expensive, slow to re-process, and don't persist across different interfaces (e.g., moving from VS Code to the web interface). To move from Chatbots to true Agents, we need to solve the state problem. The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is often described as a way to "connect AI to tools."
